title: AT&T Touts AI, Fiber Edge and Business Growth at Citi Conference
excerpt: AT&T (NYSE:T) executives said the company’s multiyear investment strategy has improved its network assets, reduced leverage and positioned its connectivity b...
content_html:
Key Points

  • Interested in AT&T Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

  • AT&T says its multiyear strategy is paying off after more than $150 billion in investment, divestitures and debt reduction, strengthening its fiber and spectrum assets. The company expects double-digit EPS growth, 3%–4% EBITDA growth this year and to return about 100% of free cash flow to shareholders.

  • Business connectivity is showing renewed momentum, with advanced-connectivity revenue growing nearly 2% year over year in the second quarter. AT&T is targeting small and midsize businesses, enterprises expanding AI workloads and public-sector customers, while investing in 400-gigabit capacity, security and network intelligence.

  • AT&T is emphasizing converged wireless and broadband services to reduce churn and increase customer value, while raising some prices with limited churn impact. The company also expects to retire copper infrastructure by the end of the decade, reducing maintenance and operating costs.

  • Intel's ASML Milestone Gives Investors a New Reason to Revisit the Stock

AT&T (NYSE:T) executives said the company's multiyear investment strategy has improved its network assets, reduced leverage and positioned its connectivity businesses for further growth, while highlighting opportunities in business services, artificial intelligence-related demand and converged wireless and broadband offerings.

Speaking at a Citi event, Chief Financial Officer Pascal Desroches said the company faced significant challenges when he and Chief Executive Officer John Stankey took their roles, including a weaker mid-band spectrum position, a predominantly DSL broadband footprint, declining DirecTV operations, the need to reposition Time Warner for direct-to-consumer distribution, and more than $150 billion in debt.

→ Morgan Stanley Eyes Good Things Ahead for Meta After $18 Billion Legal Settlement

  • AST SpaceMobile Stock Soared 12%—This Was the Catalyst

Desroches credited AT&T's divestitures of DirecTV and Time Warner, along with a reduced dividend, with enabling the company to reinvest in its core operations. He said AT&T has invested more than $150 billion over the past five years and now has what he described as the nation's largest fiber broadband network and its strongest spectrum position to date.

"We did all this while continuing to rightsize our cost base and take down our leverage," Desroches said. He added that the company has guided for double-digit earnings-per-share growth this year and plans to return about 100% of free cash flow to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.
